summary: Adds an admin endpoint that deletes one user by id and a purge endpoint that deletes a list of users.

findings.title: Delete user route lacks admin check
findings.problem: The DELETE /users/:id route omits the requireAdmin middleware that its sibling admin routes use. Any caller reaching the server can delete any user by id.
findings.consequence: A non-admin caller can delete every account by stepping through user ids. This causes permanent data loss.
findings.fix: Add requireAdmin to the route before the handler.

findings.title: Purge deletions run as floating promises
findings.problem: The forEach callback is async, so the handler never awaits any removeUser call. The handler sends removed: ids.length before any deletion finishes, even when some deletions fail.
findings.consequence: removeUser throws for an unknown id, and that rejection goes unhandled because Express never sees it. Node then crashes the server process, and the client gets a wrong removed count.
findings.fix: Await Promise.all over ids.map(db.removeUser) before responding. Alternatively, use Promise.allSettled and report the count of fulfilled deletions.
findings.suggested_change:
const results = await Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => db.removeUser(id)));
  res.json({ removed: results.filter((r) => r.status === "fulfilled").length });

findings.title: New delete endpoints have no tests
findings.problem: The change adds two deletion endpoints with auth and error paths. No test exercises either endpoint.
findings.consequence: Regressions in the authorization check or the purge error handling would ship unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests covering non-admin rejection, unknown ids, and the purge removed count.
